71: Rental and move-out inspections are what usually prompt this call in Oak Harbor, and the answer is often a stretch rather than new carpet: $99 per room to start, with most rooms finishing between $99 and $180. A power stretcher takes ripples, buckles and trip spots back down flat for roughly a fifth of replacement cost. As long as the pile is still standing and you have not tired of the color, that is the better spend.
79: Start with the failure signs. Crushed traffic lanes, seams letting go, backing that crumbles when you press it, or pet odor that outlived a professional cleaning — those mean replacement. Short of that, if the pile stands and the color still suits you, a $99-per-room stretch is the fix, and it clears most landlord and housing-office walk-throughs around Oak Harbor. Send a couple of photos or put a measure on the calendar; either way you hear which job it is before any price is written.
83: For dogs and cats on Whidbey, the combination that holds up is a moisture-barrier pad under solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing. The pad does the heavy lifting: it stops an accident from reaching the subfloor, and subfloor soak-through is the source of odor no cleaner ever gets out. The fiber itself takes diluted bleach without going pale. Figure $0.65 per square foot to move up to that pad; both ride along in the van so you can compare at home.
85: Two warranties, and both are written onto your quote. The mill stands behind the carpet against wear and stain for somewhere between 10 and 25 years, depending on the grade you choose; OC Flooring's own 1-year warranty covers the workmanship. One catch worth knowing before you pick: mills often set a minimum pad grade as a condition of their coverage, which is why all three grades ride along to every Oak Harbor measure.
